action.description: Which propagation to run — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "propagate-field" pairs with propagateField: {...}).

sourceAopId.description: The ORG aop whose field definition is the source of truth.

fieldKey.description: The custom field's stable map key on the org AOP.

targets.description: Explicit array of userIds — every one must already be linked to the same org AOP as sourceAopId, or it is refused individually (the rest still run). "uniform_and_missing" — every rep whose copy already matches the org default, plus every rep who never configured the field at all; a rep whose copy genuinely diverges is silently excluded, never attempted. "org" — every rep linked to this org AOP, uniform/diverging/missing alike.

force.description: Without this, a target whose copy diverges from the org default is refused (its diff is returned, nothing is touched). With it, a diverging target is instead proposed as its own approval-gated write — one card per target, never a blanket accept for the batch. LIMIT: force:true may only be used when AT MOST ONE target in this call is diverging — if more than one is, the ENTIRE call is refused outright (nothing written, not even uniform/missing targets) with the full diverging list, because accepting one force-proposed card replays this whole call and would otherwise silently apply every other diverging target too. Call once per diverging target instead.

sourceConnectionId.description: The connection whose mapping for crmFieldName is the source of truth.

crmFieldName.description: Identifies WHICH mapping on the source connection to propagate.

sourceAopId.description: The source connection owner's AOP whose bound CRM object (a Lead, a Partner record, ...) this mapping belongs to. The object itself is resolved server-side from that AOP's boundObjectApiName — never pass a raw object name. Omit for the standard Deal mapping.

targets.description: Explicit array of userIds, or "org" for every member of your organization (excluding the source connection's own owner). Unlike propagate-field there is no "uniform_and_missing" shortcut — a mapping's "uniform" is judged by rule-shape, computed the same way for every target regardless.

force.description: Without this, a target whose existing mapping for crmFieldName diverges from the source is refused (diff returned, nothing touched). With it, it is proposed as its own approval-gated write instead. LIMIT: force:true may only be used when AT MOST ONE target in this call is diverging — if more than one is, the ENTIRE call is refused outright (nothing written, not even uniform/missing targets) with the full diverging list, because accepting one force-proposed card replays this whole call and would otherwise silently apply every other diverging target too. Call once per diverging target instead.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.
